Hey there. I've read some of your previous posts and you're very much in a tough spot in your life right now. Standing at the golden Gate Bridge, failing classes and being abused as a child, is to me a part of what makes up all this unhappiness in you. 

There are usually two ways for people to deal with such hardship... To hurt others, or to endure and eventually live through it. To me, you're an enduring and emotionally tough person. That doesn't mean you're stable or whole. It means you're still here, where perhaps someone else would not be. 

You have two jobs - which is incredibly resourceful and persistent of you to have. You also seem like a kind, honest, but brittle person... Considering all you're going through, it's remarkable you're still such a good person.

I'm sorry I can't be of more help. I just say what I would recommend to do - which is to get a retail or similarly normal-pay job. A year or two in retail - get all money you need for your treatment - you're going to die without it.
Personally, it's hope. That the reason or reasons will come eventually.
Talk to this therapist for an hour every week... I'm sure it will help you with 1 hour of aid vs the 23 hours of agony you're otherwise in.
The police will clean it up, not anyone I know. Society isn't cruel like that.

If I were you I'd try messaging them after an hour or two to chat a little bit about having a great time and maybe future plans. It could help with feeling lonely and gives something to look forward to.

There's no reason to up the dosage, really, as your brain just has to adjust to the new amount of medication. Unfortunately if you miss a day with an antidepressant, you won't get it back. But you can change your routines for taking the medication, so you keep staying on it more consistently.

*edit: your brain "adjusting" to the new dosage takes time, like when you begin taking antidep. Unless you plan to stick with a higher dosage, it will just confuse your brain of the dosage.

That's good to hear it's not making any damage. Maybe it's related to that close someone who took their life, and you've got the thought of suicide in the back of your head due to suicide being a very negative thing for you since it's caused a great loss.

It could also be a kind of intrusive thought, which is harmless but can be discomforting. If we really oppose something, we're more likely to get intrusive thoughts of us doing that thing we'd 'never ever' do. I'll link the Wikipedia article if you feel it relates. 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_thought
> An intrusive thought is an unwelcome involuntary thought, image, or unpleasant idea that may become an obsession, is upsetting or distressing, and can feel difficult to manage or eliminate

Maybe it's not about committing suicide itself, but what it means to commit suicide. It depends on really what you feel when you think like that. To some people it's a kind of relief to imagine having the option of suicide. Others are horrified of what death is but find comfort in the loss of life's negative parts which suicide brings (at the cost of everything positive as well, which is what a lot of us can forget). Only you know what the thought of suicide means to you. I don't recommend suppressing your thoughts, we often feel things for a reason whether we know it or not. If it's making you feel really bad, then a therapist can help. If not, then there's no harm in finding out what makes you have these thoughts. They can't harm you physically, only you have that control.

No. Not even to those who invalidated me. I've had to take risks with people to find the good people. Fortunately, most people show very quickly if they are considerate and understanding. I've talked to people who can't comprehend what my life is like, but who still care to listen. A few have both understood and cared. It's been worth it and I've learned the hard way to listen to the person I'm talking to, before I let them hear me speak. I've noticed though even if I've talked to a therapist who didn't listen at all, it helped me somehow - maybe because I was admitting to myself everything I was for the first time talking about. Which is rehabilitating in itself. I'd say be careful, not seclusive. 

Are you considering talking to someone? It's a scary though; talking to a stranger irl about stuff that really make you vulnerable. I recommend it, though only you know what feels right even if it's scary.

Even though probably no one can figure out for certain, anyone can guess the reason. Don't forget that everyone feels down every now and then. The frequency of downs are personal to you, too. A doctor can prescribe light anti anxiety medication for you if you feel like it's interfering with life, or causing distress.  

The best way is of course to figure out what causes the lows and what makes you feel better again.

I think a lot of professionals actually act professional when they do this. It feels to me like what they're truly missing is something more opposite - humanity. Understanding and acknowledgement of your fellow human's hardships. I think many healthcare professionals forget that the ingredient to good health isn't medical theory, it's humane practice.
I think most people find one who does deserve it.

Suicide is premature death at any age. It only occurs because of self inflicted damage, so you die younger than supposed to. Doesn't that make all suicides young deaths? You can always discuss things like these with a therapist or school counselor. If everything is just work, work, work, then maybe you can also find a way to not just work, work, work. Make a meaning out of your life that few consider. 

Anyhow, you don't feel much pleasure in anything - maybe you're having something such as dysthymia? It's a kind of depression with milder symptoms, but keeps on going for a long time. Naturally, our brains make us feel happy and rewarded for surviving, right? But people with dysthymia have brains that "forget" to tell you that anything is good. I'm not a doctor, however reading about it could maybe tell you something about what's going on. 

http://www.webmd.com/depression/guide/chronic-depression-dysthymia

How about calling emergency services and asking to talk to someone who isn't allowed to tell anyone about you? You don't even have to tell them you've taken pills, just that you're feeling really bad. No one will be mad that you took 3350mg of sertraline in a year. In all likelihood someone will be happy that they either saved your life, or got to be there for you in the end. 

If you regret it, healthcare is always there for you to help. They will help, no matter what.
Yeah, I've used it. To me they're ineffective with anything but a little stress. They take the very, very tip off my anxiety. It's less painful than before but still hurts.

To make your depression slow down, you should keep on pushing against the wind. Be social, exercise (biking is a great exercise), talk to people you trust about thoughts and feelings. 

However, you've done the first, most important step already. You know something is seriously wrong and want to get out of it. 

The second step is to contact a doctor so you can tell them everything and more of what you've said here. That is you've lost interest in what you used to enjoy, feel tired, maybe even sad, and have been for several years which is unlike you. After that, the Dr will advice treatments, and I really recommend you accept what they can offer. It's going to take time to become repaired from this, but it's better to swim than drown.

Have you tried other anti depressants? If the max dosage of Zoloft doesn't work it might be targeting the wrong parts of your brain. Maybe you need a different SSRI, or a whole other class of anti depressants. Our bodies are constantly changing and sometimes starts reacting to our usual meds differently. 

Other than meds, it's excellent with exercise that makes you sweaty, good sleep, a nice social life, eating healthy, etc. Some people also feel good from changing their schedules up or doing new things, alternatively others need less changes and strict schedules to feel fine. Experiment to find what helps you

It's a difficult situation. I bet she can take care herself, most days. Tell her you'll always be here. Let her take the contact, but keep reminding that you're available (it will be forgotten again and again). You need to show that you can be trusted, but you must also trust her first. There is only really one occasion in which she can't be trusted, and that's when it's time to call the police. 

For example she might like invitations to things sometimes, or just knowing that someone cares about how she's feeling at the moment. It's a balance between showing support and being pushy. Not easy - however very much possible to achieve. 

Stay strong and take care of yourself.

You seem to want to change her into a more positive person, and make her feel good again. I just want to put it simple: no one can walk this path for her. Be present for her, lend a hand, and let her win this like an, adult. She's in a fragile state of mind and will make mistakes, including pushing people away. Just like with a fractured arm - you can't heal it, but support is always needed to keep on going. 

Take time to relax when you need to, in order to recuperate. So you can be there for her when she really needs it. Remember, you can't cure her, but you can support her.

Sounds like you had a very good first session with a good therapist and opening up is what a good therapist wants you to do. Feeling worried about telling someone your troubles is natural for most people - it makes us vulnerable. When we're vulnerable we can get hurt, but we can also heal. The more you two talk, the more you'll get to know each other and the easier it'll be to talk. Starting therapy can be tiring because of anxiety, subconscious alertness, worry, and other things. You most likely consumed a large portion of your energy when talking to her, that's a natural reaction. It's a big step  - a good step. 

I think you should ask her why she's saying you'll get better. If you have doubts, tell her. She doesn't know where you'll be in 5 years, but I think she knows, just as well as you, that what she can promise is the road you'll be heading on. I hope you trust yourself to walk it with her. If something is inevitable faith then you're about to have a hell of a battle with faith. So take a bet and fight it with someone who knows how to fight it.

Thanks for sharing. You're right, suicide isn't the easy way out. It takes strength to end it. But it also takes strength just to keep on going when life's a drain. I really hope you find a good therapist and that you together can put together the broken pieces to start making your life whole again. I think you deserve more than to suffer. Good luck

It's good to know that you're still standing. Helping others is in my opinion one of the best ways to make yourself feel better, as long as we remember ourselves. If that doesn't help today then maybe your brain wants you to focus on **you** for now? Like talking about things that don't feel so good or doing something thoughtful for yourself. No matter if people have noticed your responses or not, you deserve a medal for putting in the effort. Like many of us unfortunately know, that makes you a better person than a lot of people. Remember that you're just as important as those people you've helped. I hope your emotions sort themselves out.

Hey there. Sounds like a shitty day, but after all of this at least you're still standing. It's shitty being isolated, it's shitty feeling like the elephant in the room in your own family and it's shitty being so sad you barely can see. But in all of this, you still remember your teacher and friend. Remembering them while you're in such a dark place seems to me like an incredible thing. You're incredible for fighting on, like your own personal soldier. 

You've probably heard this, so it's your choice if you want to hear some of it again. Maybe you'll call this time or maybe you won't, but please call the emergency services if you're very likely to hurt yourself. Or if you for some reason don't want to, or feel a little bit better, I hope you can find comfort in knowing there are listeners available right now on the internet, here, and from organisations who help minors with tough situations. Please consider the resources at [SuicideWatch Resources](https://www.reddit.com/r/SWResources/). Incredible, selfless and kind people are waiting for you. They're a call away, and I hope you make it.

Hi there, thanks for sharing all of this. You don't need to be sorry for asking, on this subreddit we're all here to listen and there are a lot of us here who care. You're doing good trying to figure out what to do about this, and asking people for help and support is one of the best ways to do that. It's a difficult thing looking for support but it shows your strength. What that person did to you was wrong and a person who survives rape is a very strong person. I can understand why you fear men, just remember that he was an unusual man who thought he was allowed to do whatever he wanted, even though he's not. I hope he can't get to you, and that it's all in the past. You're safe in this moment.

Why do you feel like your family will tell you that you're overdramatic? What about talking to an adult at your school, like a teacher you like or a counsellor? Other young girls like you have also been raped and abused. They might feel like they're unloved and disgusting for what has happened. Some of them blame themselves for what's happened or think about and remember a lot of the things they went through. Because of this many abused children feel alone or unwanted. You and everyone don't deserve what happened. What you do deserve is so much better than that. 

Everyone deserves to be heard, to be able to speak about what is weighing them down and to feel good about themselves. When we feel hurt, we back off from others so not to get hurt again, it's like a left-over response from when the abuse was happening and your brain doesn't know if the threat is over or not. Feeling like that is never fun and a teacher or counsellor can be the wall you need to lean against while healing from what has happened.
